# Piggles — pane ratings

**Version:** 3.04
**Author:** Brandon Korous
**Last Updated:** 2026-09-30

Every pane in the Piggles console, scored on **Design** and **Ease** as the ten
personas open them. How and when to score is RULE #6 in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md);
this file is where the numbers live.

**Scored so far: ALL 335 console panes**, plus **10 of 30** in the non-console list below (the sites, the sign-in, the chrome), plus the status bar, which is console chrome rather
than a pane and so has no row below — its score lives in
[issue 018](issues/018-two-unsaved-changes-was-neither-two-nor-changes.md) (Ease 6 → 8). Nor is the NOTIFICATIONS BELL, which is
chrome that draws sentences somebody else wrote: the one notice on the platform read
"The Everyday Tee is out of stock" about a product with 35 versions, 1 of them at
zero and 75 tees on the shelf, because a seeded automation named the product on an
event about a variant
([861](issues/861-one-size-ran-out-and-the-bell-said-the-product-was-gone.md)). A
pane's score says nothing about the copy a notification puts inside it. The eight menus in the
chrome are likewise not panes and have no rows; what opening every one of them with a MOUSE found
is in [issue 279](issues/279-the-menus-had-never-been-clicked.md) — they had never been clicked, because [277] meant
none of them could be. Nor is the state a pane shows when its MODULE is off: chrome shared by all
328 of them, and it read "something went wrong reaching the server" over a Try again that could
never work until [457](issues/457-a-switched-off-app-read-as-a-broken-server.md). Nor is a pane's
TAB LABEL, which is chrome the pane does not draw: 52 surfaces across the two consoles wrote their
own, which pinned 8 of them to a word used nowhere else in the console
([458](issues/458-a-pane-that-named-itself-in-the-wrong-language.md)) — so a row below may be
scored 8 for a screen whose tab was saying something else entirely. Nor, until
[650](issues/650-on-my-phone-the-buttons-are-circles-with-no-words-and-one-of-them-stops-my-stock.md),
was a pane's toolbar reliably operable by thumb: 35 controls across 26 files carried their only name
in a `hidden` span, which `display:none` removes from the accessibility tree — so at 360px they were
unlabeled glyphs, three of them side by side on one toolbar. Any row scored on Ease before
2026-09-18 was scored against a narrow width that read worse than the number says. And any row
scored before
[655](issues/655-download-what-you-have-handed-her-a-web-page.md) whose pane offers a DOWNLOAD was
scored without that button being pressed: every one of them saved the console's own HTML under the
filename it promised, and `inventory.stock.import` carried a 9 for Ease on the strength of reading
the endpoint behind its primary control rather than clicking it. Reading the code that a button
calls is not using the button. [[feedback_test_as_a_business_owner]] Nor is the SEARCH BOX at the top of
every screen a pane, and it had never been typed into with a record's name in mind: it could reach 3 of
Juniper Row's 86 records and answered "Nothing in your records matches" about the other 83
([664](issues/664-the-search-box-had-never-read-my-records.md)). Any row below scored on how findable its
records are was scored against a box that had not read them. Update that line as rows fill in — it is the
denominator, and a rating file that does not show what it has not looked at is
the same lie as an empty issue list.

**COUNT THE UNSCORED ROWS WITH A PARSER, NOT A GREP.** Act 281 tracked what was
left with `grep -c "| —      | —     | —"`, which reported 21 when the real
number was 52: the column widths differ between the per-app tables, so that
pattern's padding only matches some of them, and the non-console table at the
foot has six columns rather than seven so it never matched at all. A whole app's
worth of panes — every Partner screen, every My Team screen, all four AI ones —
was invisible to the thing counting what was left. Split each row on `|`, accept
both widths, and compare the Design cell to an em dash.
[[feedback_structural_checks_go_blind]]

## The two axes

| Axis       | The question                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Design** | Is it on-system and well-composed? Silica components and tokens, real color doing real work (not a grey screen), hierarchy from scale and weight, holds at 360px, and the waiting / empty / error states all present and right |
| **Ease**   | Could this owner do the job without help? Findable, one home per concern, the data she needs already on screen, no dead ends, words she uses, an obvious next step — and reachable by keyboard and by thumb                    |

Both are reported. A beautiful pane nobody can operate is not an 8; a plain pane
that gets the job done in two taps is not a 4. Where one number is wanted, quote
the lower.

**Score it in both themes and at 360px, or do not score it.** A number taken in
one theme at one width is a guess about the other three — and dark mode is where
the largest defect in this build's history was hiding, unreachable by every
automated check.

| Score | Means                                                         |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 9–10  | Nothing to fix. A 10 needs a reason written in the gap column |
| 7–8   | Right, with named nits                                        |
| 5–6   | Works; she needed a second look or a second attempt           |
| 3–4   | She got there by persistence, or it looks unfinished          |
| 1–2   | She would stop, ask somebody, or leave                        |

**The deductions are the point.** Every scored row carries a **gap to 10** — the
specific thing that would raise it. Anything in that column which is a real
defect becomes an issue and is fixed on the spot (RULE #3), then the row is
re-scored keeping both numbers: `5 → 8`.

A pane no persona reached stays `—`. Never infer a score from the code, from a
sibling pane, or from the fact that it typechecks.

## How to fill a row

| Column    | What goes in it                                                                                                                  |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pane      | as printed. "depends on what is open" is a pane whose title is computed from the record it holds — a product, an invoice, a page |
| Key       | the surface key — what the address bar and the launcher use                                                                      |
| Design    | `1`–`10`, or `4 → 8` after a fix                                                                                                 |
| Ease      | same                                                                                                                             |
| Gap to 10 | one short phrase. If it is a defect, add `#NNN`                                                                                  |
| Persona   | who opened it — `P03`. Several may score the same pane; keep the latest and note the earlier in the gap column if it differed    |

## Panes that are deliberately absent

Eleven surfaces are excluded from Piggles by `hiddenSurfaces` — sparx's
marketplace, its module-priced settings screen, its reseller programme, and the
platform bill that belongs on getpiggles. They are not listed below and are not
scored. **If a persona ever reaches one, that is a `major` issue, not a rating.**

One pane already fails that test before any run: `partner.bootcamp.detail`
appears below under "Not reachable from any app rail" because its list screen is
hidden and it is not — see [issue 002](issues/002-bootcamp-detail-still-reachable.md).
It is listed rather than quietly dropped, because a pane nobody can name is a
pane nobody removes.

Every one of the thirteen checks had two stored names. Windows a business thinks in (7/30/90), headline totals, per-account rows, top posts that open the post, and a "post around here" panel drawn from THIS business's own numbers rather than an industry average — with the file arguing that an average tells a parts distributor in Utah what it tells a bakery in Lisbon. A number a platform never reported shows as a dash, never a made-up zero, which is [[feedback_never_present_absence_as_measurement]] done right without being asked. Ease 7: the empty state told her to "open a post you have already sent and hit Refresh numbers", which names something she has never had — and this pane was ALREADY calling the overview twice for the avatars, so it had the answer ([459]). Now splits the two reasons a chart is empty. The charts themselves are unscored: no posts exist to draw.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | P03     |
| Posts                       | `social.queue`       | 8      | 8                 | Scored by P03, empty. Preview TILES rather than table rows, and the file argues the case: a row spends its width on one line of text and crops the picture to a chip, so a screen of posts reads as a spreadsheet in which no two are distinguishable. Every cover is forced to one ratio so the grid reads as a grid. A pipeline strip across the top is both the glance and the filter, and "Needs a look" is the only count that earns a warning color. Same first-run miss as the calendar and fixed with it ([459]): its one action was "New post", which dead-ended at the composer. It now offers **Connect an account**, which is the composer's own answer one screen earlier. Its tab said "Posts" correctly throughout — this is one of the panes that proved [458], because it sat beside three that did not.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | P03     |

### Campaigns — 2 panes

| Pane                      | Key                 | Design | Ease  | Gap to 10                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Persona |
| ------------------------- | ------------------- | ------ | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| (depends on what is open) | `funnels.campaign`  | 9      | 6 → 9 | The best-written editor in this console, and it had a row of dead controls nobody explained. "The steps — in order, from the first thing somebody does to the outcome you want. Renaming a step keeps everything it has already recorded" is a data model taught in two sentences; "Where people come in", "What counts as success" and "When to give up on somebody" are headings a shop owner can act on, and the last one argues its own case ("somebody who starts and then goes quiet is not a failure yet, but at some point they are gone"). Ease 6 for four things, all of them the screen keeping to itself something the FILE already knew. The last step's dropdown, both arrows and its delete were greyed with no reason given — it is the outcome and must stay last, said in the comments and nowhere a person could read it. The step-kind dropdown had an `aria-label` and no visible label, so the screen reader was told what it was for and the person looking at it was not. The page hint said "leave this empty to count visits to the campaign's landing page" when a landing page is a server field NOTHING in either console sets, while the same pane's Turn it on button refuses for exactly that reason. And `disabled` stopped at the Add a step button, so a viewer could rewrite every step and find out at Save. The report half printed a bare "Loading…" and, on a failure, one sentence with no retry. [829](issues/829-a-locked-control-that-never-says-why.md) | P03     |
| Campaigns                 | `funnels.campaigns` | 8      | 6 → 8 | A list that earns its shape: rows rather than tiles because a campaign has no picture and what tells two apart is the name, the state and the ladder, with the strip of step names showing the SHAPE without one request per row. The empty state teaches the whole idea in one sentence ("somebody finds your page, leaves their details, and eventually buys something or books you in") and the status badges carry a NOTE each rather than a bare word — Draft is "Not counting anyone yet", Paused is "Keeping what it already recorded, and not adding to it". Ease 6: the bar said nothing at all on its left, so "how many are there" meant counting rows; a failed read did an early `return` before the toolbar, dropping the search, the filters and New campaign with it — the shape `pane-load-error.tsx` names in its own header as the thing never to do; and the no-match state told a person who had pressed a filter chip to "try different words" they had never typed. It now says **1 campaign**, or **0 of 1 campaign** when a filter is hiding some, names whichever thing is hiding them in that chip's own words, and hands her the button that undoes it. [829](issues/829-a-locked-control-that-never-says-why.md)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | P03     |

The balances table already holds a phone (327px of table in a 329px scrollport, overflow 0), and the history list reads in plain words ("Refund kept as credit", "Spent on an order"). Held off 8 by the grey `neutral` on every negative ledger badge, which is the one place the list distinguishes money out from money in and spends no color doing it (RULE #4; it joins the 585 waiting on Brandon rather than being repainted on a guess). **Ease 8, and it was 4 before act 262** — four faults, three of them hit while doing the one thing the pane is for ([735](issues/735-a-grant-you-cannot-undo.md)). A grant was **permanent**: `amountCents` is refined positive, `grant` and the ledger read were the only two endpoints, and one mistyped digit put $1,850 on a customer with nothing in the console able to reach it — while `deltaCents` stayed signed and the history below drew a minus sign for a line nothing could write. There is a **Take some back instead** path now, audited, noted, refused above the balance and refused again before the press. The customer picker reported a **503 as "No customer matches that. Try a different word."** (measured: seventeen of them, about a shop that had the customer all along) while the card three inches below it said "Could not load balances" correctly, in the same file. It could not tell **two customers called Priya Anand** apart, because it drew the name and an email one of them does not have; and it never drew a company at all, since `/v1/crm/customers` returns `companyName` and only the balances endpoint had been taught the rename — so the same `CustomerLite` was blank on one side and a trade buyer read as "A customer". And the panel did not focus its own search box, so the first word typed into it went nowhere. **Not 9:** every grant is still hardcoded USD, which is right for this tenant and latent for the next one. Shows the real people now. Collapses well at 390px (Shopper · Items · Value) and the collapsed toolbar keeps a count badge so the active filter is never silently hidden. The tab the pane is NAMED for then turned out to have been empty on every tenant since commerce shipped: nothing ran the abandonment marker, so `abandoned_at` was null on every basket, all time ([283]). A sweep on a `*/10` CronJob supplies the clock the feature was missing, and her own threshold field — previously read by nothing — now decides when a basket lands here. Running it for real exposed two more: a marked basket 404'd on add-to-cart and on checkout and could never be recovered ([284], **blocker**), and the marker overwrote **Last active** with its own clock, flattening the only column that ranks the queue ([285]). Both fixed and confirmed on the screen. Remaining gaps: `cart.abandoned` now fires and nothing subscribes, so a basket landing here is not yet a shopper being followed up; and a basket that came back once can never be flagged again, which needs a decision on what `recovered_at` means ([284]). Both fixed. Act 7 then found three money defects on this one pane: a refund settled on a return never reached the order, which went on offering to refund the whole thing again ([222](issues/222-she-gave-42-back-and-the-order-offered-to-give-it-all-back-again.md)); noting a cheque number made the order un-refundable, because the note was written into the gateway-reference field ([223](issues/223-writing-the-cheque-number-down-made-the-order-unrefundable.md)); and the pane had nowhere to start a return at all ([219](issues/219-there-was-no-way-to-start-a-return.md)). All fixed. It now carries a **Coming back** section and reads Part paid · Paid so far · Given back, with the returned line marked. **P03, the standing RLS check:** an order that could not load never resolved at all -- a spinner with no end, because a refused request scheduled a retry that was then held ([287](issues/287-the-order-that-would-not-load-just-said-just-a-moment-forever.md)). It now reaches a state, and a record that is not this business's says so rather than blaming the server ([286](issues/286-the-console-blamed-the-server-for-a-product-that-was-never-hers.md)). Checked in dark, light and at 360px. **Acts 101-102, Asking for payment.** The pane gained the section that bills the order, and reading it back found three sentences that were not true: the button said **Send an invoice** and only made one, the section said "the invoices you have **sent**", and every row printed **Sent 7 Sep** off the date the document was CREATED -- telling her a customer had a bill that never left the building. It now says Make an invoice, and each row carries the real send ("Sent Sep 7, 2026 to anneliese.vogt@example.com") or "Not sent yet" ([438](issues/438-she-shipped-the-goods-and-had-no-way-to-ask-for-the-money.md)). Holds at 9: the section reads in her words, refuses by name, and hides the button where an invoice would be wrong. | **Re-scored down and back on P03, act 308, on the Sold by section.** The commission calculation returns SIX outcomes and this console's type listed five, so the sixth fell through the switch to the catch-all and said **“That sale could not be found”** about a sale on the screen with a named person credited to it. The missing one is the worst to miss: they ARE on commission, but their rate started after this sale. The shared calculation keeps that apart from “no rate” on purpose, and its own comment says why — the two are fixed in opposite ways, and it records the harm it was written to stop: an owner who had just set a 7.5% rate being told to go and set a rate. Now the sentence carries both dates, because the comparison IS the message, and the remedy that actually works: pay rates may not overlap, so adding an earlier one is refused and remove-then-re-add is the real path. **Ease 9 → 5 → 9.** Not yet hit by anybody — one commission rate exists platform-wide and it is not hers — and it opens the first time any owner sets a rate today and recalculates an older sale. Found by MEASUREMENT rather than clicking, chasing issue 865's class: 44 of 1,219 shapes declared in both consoles differ by a field, three of them with this console behind ([871](issues/871-her-console-did-not-know-the-sixth-answer.md)).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | **Re-scored down and back on P03, act 310, on the two things this pane could not do.** The **Notes** section prints two headings, “From the customer” and “Your team’s note”, and rendered nothing at all while both were empty. Both were empty on **every order ever placed: 0 of 122**, because nothing on the platform could write either. Not the console, not the till, not checkout, not a channel import. `PATCH /v1/orders/:id` takes four things; the two addresses were wired here with a paragraph headed “WHY THIS WAS MISSING AND WHY THAT MATTERED”, and the two notes beside them were not. **Truth 9 → 6 → 9**, because a heading saying a customer told her something, over a field no customer on the platform could ever fill, is a false claim about her own records. It is back at 9 with the shop’s note a box on this pane and a box at checkout for the buyer, stored on the session before payment so a redirecting gateway cannot swallow it ([874](issues/874-the-notes-on-an-order-could-never-be-written.md)). **Ease 9 → 5 → 9**: money recorded by hand could never be un-recorded. `POST /v1/orders/:id/payments/:paymentId/void` has always existed, is idempotent, recomputes `amountPaid` and the buyer’s lifetime total and writes an audit entry, and nothing in either console called it; `voided_at` is NULL on all 33 payments. Ten of the seventeen hand-taken payments on the platform are hers, and a counter is exactly where the money goes against the wrong order. | Return                    | `commerce.return.detail`                | 8             | 2 → 8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Every move on a return lived here and **nothing anywhere could create one** ([219](issues/219-there-was-no-way-to-start-a-return.md)); an exchange could then only be ended by refunding a customer owed nothing ([220](issues/220-an-even-exchange-could-only-be-ended-by-refunding-it.md)); a return whose sale had been deleted still offered to approve it and buy a carrier label ([225](issues/225-twenty-returns-for-sales-that-do-not-exist.md)). All fixed. Settling now follows what the customer asked, and a swap ends **Swapped · $0.00 moved**. Two more then came out of driving it end to end. The screen asking WHICH version to send showed name, code and price and no count, on a return whose customer had written _"a size up in Oat if you have one"_ — she answered from memory and was wrong with six on the shelf, and the picker opened alphabetically over the whole catalog, leading a knitwear swap on signet rings ([450](issues/450-she-chose-what-to-send-without-being-shown-what-she-had.md), fixed: the returned product first, every row reading N to sell / None left / Not counted). And the swap reached NOBODY — the received email promises _"we will email you again the moment your exchange is on its way"_ and no such email existed, while the deny dialog said _"they are told the reason you give here"_ over a turn-down that published nothing ([448](issues/448-two-of-the-three-ways-a-return-ends-tell-the-customer-nothing.md), blocker, fixed across the whole lifecycle). [453](issues/453-the-replacement-went-out-with-no-way-to-follow-it.md) closed the gap that email left: the replacement had no delivery record of ITS own, so a shop could say "on its way" and nothing more, on a platform whose ordinary shipping confirmation leads with the tracking number because that is what the recipient opened it for. Not an order fulfillment — that path caps each line at what is still owed and the line was fulfilled once already, so forcing it would double-count and email "your order has shipped" about an order that shipped weeks ago. The return owns its parcel instead: `commerce_return_labels` already held one going the other way, so it gained a DIRECTION rather than a second table gaining six identical columns. Asked at two moments because that is when the answer exists — at settle time when the parcel has already gone, and through **Say how it went out** when it has not, which is the ordinary way round. Never both, so a customer gets one email rather than two saying the same thing. Four neighbours came with it: the email resolver read "the newest label on this return" and would have sent somebody wanting to POST a parcel to a tracking page for one already sent; NEITHER console rendered `labels` at all, so the prepaid label has always been fetched and drawn nowhere; the carrier list was one screen away from a third copy; and the schema comment listing return statuses never learned `exchanged`. [449](issues/449-the-sparx-console-cannot-settle-a-swap-at-all.md) closed the same hole in the sparx console — a port that turned out to be four things, because the status line there told every swap to give the money back, the picker drew no version names at all (the option values have always been on the wire and that console typed them away, so a fuel injector's two versions differed only by price), and a swapped return matched no filter chip in either console. **Driving it produced the two findings that matter most on this pane.** [451](issues/451-every-other-product-in-the-swap-picker-said-not-counted.md): the counts I added the day before come from ONE request for the product that came back, and the picker lists the whole catalog — so every other row read **Not counted** whether it was or not, which is a claim about the shop's records made about a product nobody asked after. I had confirmed that screen and read my own evidence backwards. Fixed by making the counts carry the product they answer for, so a row outside it gets no badge: four answers, and the fourth is silence. [452](issues/452-the-goods-came-back-and-then-existed-on-no-screen.md): after settling a swap the way a busy shop would, the database showed **one** movement — the replacement going out. The faulty part that came back never went anywhere and appeared on no screen in the product, because restocking is driven by inspection rows, the returns bench is BUILT by joining inspections, and the console stops offering the form once a return is settled. Silent, permanent, and money. A settled return now still accepts the condition of its goods — condition is a fact about the goods, not the money — without ever walking backwards into a stage that offers to pay twice; on screen the goods went from invisible to **1 to decide**. **Then I drove [453] instead of reading it, and two minutes of clicking found two more** ([454](issues/454-a-code-on-one-screen-a-shelf-nobody-stocked.md)). The Parcels card printed the stored carrier code, so her own screen said "usps" and the same value rode the event into her customer's email — a defect this platform had ALREADY found and fixed for the ordinary shipping confirmation, whose map carries a comment saying a customer was told their parcel went by "usps". The old bug in a new place, a day later. The picker was a fourth copy of the words and had already drifted, saying "Someone else" where the shared map said "Another courier" about the same parcel on the order handover screen. And the toast after settling a swap said "One came back on the shelf" when the database showed ONE movement, the replacement going out: nothing was inspected, and goods go back on a shelf only once an inspection says they are fit to sell, so the sentence was true for a shop that checks the goods and false for one that does not — contradicting [452]'s card directly below it in the same second. The console could not tell because `settleExchange` returned only the return id, so it guessed and printed the guess as fact; it now returns `unitsRestocked` and the sentence is built from it, saying with zero that nothing has been written down yet about what came back. The link to the customer's order wears commerce's hue through a nested `ModuleScope`, which is the cross-module rule done without being asked. **The defect was in the first row of that list.** "Reached the supplier" was drawn from `createdAt`, which the schema defaults to `now()` on a row whose status defaults to `pending` — so it asserted the supplier had the order at the moment nothing had been sent, directly above "Sent to the supplier: Not yet". Two rows four inches apart contradicting each other, with the top one making the stronger claim. It says **Lined up to send**. Also the waiting state was a bare `<PaneWaiting>` outside the shell (a bare `<p>Loading…</p>` in sparx, with the failure outside the pane too). | How many you have           | `commerce.product.stock`                          | 8         | 7 → 8                                 | The best-written pane in the stock module: a card per version, a row per place, and the states in her words. "Not counted anywhere yet" is exact and rare — most software renders a missing measurement as a zero, and this one says _"Nobody has said how many of this version you have, so your website sells it without limit"_ with **Record a count** beside it. What it did not do was say so at the TOP. The summary — written so "the question 'do I have any' is settled before anyone reads a single row" — read **78 to sell** on a shirt where five of twenty versions were selling with no number behind them, and the news was on the twentieth card down ([444](issues/444-she-added-a-color-and-five-shirts-went-on-sale-with-no-count-behind-them.md), fixed: the all-uncounted message now has a mixed-case twin naming the count and the first three codes). Then two more, both fixed: **Record a count** opened on the first location alphabetically — Fulfillment Center — when every unit Juniper Row owns is at Main Warehouse, and it did not remember the one just used, so counting five versions of one product meant changing it five times ([445](issues/445-the-count-form-opens-on-a-building-she-does-not-use.md); it now reads this version's own place, then the place last counted at, then where the rest of the product is). And the mixed-case message itself named too much: it counted every uncounted version rather than the ones whose setting is going unhonored, so a shop of memberships and downloads was told to go and count things that are unlimited on purpose ([446](issues/446-the-uncounted-band-told-her-to-count-33-things-that-cannot-run-out.md)). Act 244: that summary card printed the row beneath it VERBATIM whenever a product has a single variant in a single place — the same three figures and the same three words, 150px apart — which is **64 of the 188 products with any stock at all** ([699](issues/699-the-same-figure-twice-and-an-alarm-on-neither.md)). It is now gated on there being more than one row to roll up. The reorder line mixed sentence punctuation with list punctuation ("…runs down. · costs you $18.55 each") and reads as one list now. Both buttons on the card were driven: **Set a reorder rule** opened a three-field form, took 12 / 40 / 14 from empty, registered the leave-guard, saved, and read back as "Warns at 12, then order 40 · about 14 days to arrive" | Shipment                    | `inventory.advance-ship-notices.detail`           | 9 → 8 → 9 | 8                                     | Scored by P03 on the first two notices ever recorded on the platform ([669](issues/669-both-screens-told-me-to-do-it-on-the-other-one.md)). **Design 9, the highest in Buying:** it is built around one idea and never loses it — a notice is a CLAIM, and the screen keeps the claim and the count in separate columns (They sent / Arrived) so the two can be compared rather than conflated. The pre-delivery banner refuses to say the notice matched, because "nothing has been compared, because nothing has arrived" is a different statement from "it agreed", and printing 0 would read as the second. "No dispatch date given" sits where a date would, rather than an em-dash. **Ease 4 → 8:** the pane was unreachable — nothing on the platform could create a notice — and once one existed, booking the delivery left it saying "Nothing has been checked in against this yet" over a table whose Arrived column said 4, with the button still offering to book the same delivery again. Worst of the four: it compared the notice with the order line's LIFETIME received, so a second note for the last 2 of 6 read **"4 more than the notice — worth checking before it is paid for twice"** over a delivery that matched to the unit. | Waiting for stock           | `inventory.backorders`                            | 8         | 8 → 9                                 | Scored by P03 with nothing owed. Design 8: the toolbar carries the answer (**"Nothing owed"**) rather than a title, and the empty state tells her apart from a quiet week: **"Nobody has ever waited on stock. Nothing has ever had to wait for stock. Somebody appears here the moment you take an order the shelf cannot cover."** Ease 8: the lens select reads as five questions ("Still waiting", "No date given", "Past the date", "Stock has landed", "Everything") and the pane raises a red alert when people are waiting with NO date at all, saying who can fix it and how. Pressing **Re-check dates** on an empty account answered "Nothing changed · Every commitment already carries the best date available", which is vacuously true rather than wrong. Gap to 10: that sentence claims something about orders she does not have. **Re-scored 9 after [660](issues/660-the-pack-bench-offered-me-a-shirt-nobody-could-find.md):** its **Re-check dates** button was live on a queue that has never held a row, and pressed it answered "Every commitment already carries the best date available" — true of nothing, and read by somebody who has never taken such an order as though they had some. The pane already knew, so the button is off with the reason on it. **2026-09-18, act 241:** the item column named things by a code. `variantName` came from `ProductVariant.title`, which is null for a third of the catalogue and holds the OPTION LABEL (“White / 2XL”) for the rest, so the cell printed either a raw SKU or a size, never the product. Five services did this; one, What your stock cost you, had solved it properly and alone. It now reads the product name, the version and the code as three parts from one shared helper ([681](issues/681-five-stock-lists-showed-a-code-where-a-name-belongs.md)). **2026-09-19, act 256:** the body of both this pane and Owed called the thing a **commitment** thirteen times, which is the supply-chain word the screen NAMES were deliberately chosen to avoid - the catalog entry argues the case for the name in its own comment and the sentences underneath never got it ([725](issues/725-a-commitment-appears-here.md)). They now use the word the screens are named for.. **Fixed without a re-walk (act 315):** the promised date was drawn with a formatter that renders on the reader's own clock, which shows the DAY BEFORE for everyone west of Greenwich — a date a buyer quotes down the phone, off by one, on a screen whose own comment says getting it wrong "is how a business loses a customer twice" ([885](issues/885-a-bill-due-today-said-she-had-already-missed-it.md)). Found by measurement from the supplier invoices rather than by opening it: Juniper Row has no backorders, so the score is held rather than re-scored That gap is the thing a shop owner needs and almost nothing else shows. The **Drop** confirm names the customer and the count and says the order itself is untouched. **Found here:** the body called the thing a **commitment** eight times under a tab that says Owed ([725](issues/725-a-commitment-appears-here.md)); and an address whose id is malformed answered "the server is unreachable" over a Try again that could never work, because `paneLoadReason` had split out 404 and 5xx and left 400 and 422 in the default ([726](issues/726-a-cut-off-link-said-the-server-was-down.md)). Below `@md` the State column folds into the invoice cell rather than competing with it, which the give-cell rule asks for and this pane honors. **Ease 7:** the Due column was a countdown and nothing else — “in 20 days” on three of four rows, no date anywhere ([671](issues/671-the-money-screens-said-how-long-never-when.md)). | How a bill looks          | `invoicing.template.edit`    | 9      | 7                     | **2026-09-22, act 275 -- built this act, walked end to end.** The house editor layout, a `max-w-3xl` column of FormSection cards, and the page itself as an ordered list of blocks named in her words rather than by node type: _The top of the page_, _Who it is for_, _What they are paying for_, _The amounts_, _Your own words_. Three more came out of the walk once it opened. The **Reference name** box was editable on the three workflows the PLATFORM resolves by slug, under the words _change it only if you have a reason to_; renaming `b2b-quotes` would have minted a second copy behind her back and started printing her quotes as bills with a balance due, re-opening issues 764 and 765 from a text box ([781](issues/781-renaming-a-workflow-broke-the-platforms-own-lookup.md), fixed: the server refuses it and the field says why). The stage badges printed the schema at her -- **Quoted / Draft**, **Submitted / Draft**, **Under Review / Draft**, **Declined / Void** -- which issue 766 had fixed in the advance menu one file over and not here, where the meaning is CHOSEN ([782](issues/782-the-badge-said-draft-on-a-stage-called-quoted.md), fixed). And archiving had no undo at all: the list could FIND what she had put away and the editor offered nothing to press, under a confirm describing a reversible change ([783](issues/783-archiving-a-workflow-had-no-way-back.md), fixed: a restore endpoint in the house shape, one toolbar slot, and the confirm now says so first). 9 -- built a real two-step commission workflow end to end, dragged it, saved it, archived it, brought it back, and found it waiting in the document type picker. Every choice on this screen explains itself in a sentence in her words at the moment she makes it, and writes the consequence back under the step: _Arriving here numbers it CW-... and freezes a permanent record._ Two boxes for the step's name, one for customers and one for the team, is a distinction nobody asked for and everybody wants. | P03     |

The **State** column printed _Active_ on all six rows, because the filter defaults to Active and the server filters on it -- a badge that cannot differ, holding width the chain needed. The columns in the file are listed before you download it, "Mark these as sent" explains both settings rather than just the on state, and every connector that is not switched on says so plainly with what to do instead. Six connector rows told her to use "the export below" under a heading saying "the export above" ([471](issues/471-six-rows-pointed-below-at-something-above-them.md)). ### Not reachable from any app rail — 8 panes

**These cannot be scored by a Piggles persona, and that is the correct answer
rather than a gap.** They are sparx's RESELLER PROGRAMME — referrals,
commissions, tier, bootcamps and a listing in the sparx partner directory —
which piggles/CLAUDE.md names as a sparx product, and the default for those is
exclude. `product.tsx` hides the whole `partner.*` NAMESPACE rather than eight
keys, because the seven were written out once and the eighth was missed, so a
Piggles business could deep-link into another company's training programme
(issue #002).

Checked on 2026-09-25 by trying: `/partner/clients` as Devi lands on **"That
link doesn't open anything"**, and the launcher offers none of the eight. The
hiding holds.

Piggles HAS a Partners app. It is about the reader's own SUPPLIERS, it is built
entirely from `claims` on inventory and dropship surfaces, and every one of
those is scored in its own app's table above.

Scored `n/a` so they stop reading as work nobody has done. They want a SPARX
persona, which this file does not have.

## Not in the console, and rated anyway

The console is not the whole product. These are scored on the same two axes by
whichever persona goes through them, because a business owner does not know where
one app stops and the next begins.

**The twelve published sites are scored as sites** — would a stranger buy from,
book on, or read this one without knowing it was a test (RULE #8)? Score the site
whole, and name its weakest page in the gap column, because that is the page a
real visitor lands on. Their design is judged as **the tenant's brand**, not
against sparx's restraint rules, which do not apply to a customer's website.

| getpiggles — password reset                 | 8      | 6 → 9         | Two screens, four failure branches, and one of them found the biggest thing this act turned up: **a completed password reset did not end the other sessions.** `revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset` was never set, so better-auth read it as false — while the IN-CONSOLE password change already defaults `revokeOtherSessions` to true in both workbenches. So the product had decided what changing a password means, and the one path that exists for _somebody else knows my password_ was the path that left them signed in, for a sliding 30-day window (issue 837). Three copy faults beside it. **"Then we will sign you back in."** has never been true: the endpoint mints no session and the form pushes `/sign-in`, so she retypes the password she just chose plus a two-step code. Sending the link left the standing instruction **"Tell us the email you sign in with and we will send you a link"** above a green box saying it was already sent, with no field left and **no way to try a different address** — on a form whose own comment names a mistyped address as its accepted cost. An expired link said **"Please request a new one"** on a screen carrying no link to anywhere, while the no-token branch of the same route gets a button. And **"under 128 characters"** refused a password the server would have taken. What it gets right is a lot, and measured rather than assumed: the same answer for a known and an unknown address with **"if"** said out loud; the address normalised with the function that stored it (`  P03.Devi@Piggles.TEST  ` produced a live token for `p03.devi@piggles.test`); **"good for the next hour"** true to the second (the stored window is exactly `01:00:00`, and the email says 60 minutes); four distinct failures with four distinct sentences, all driven on screen; a too-short password that does **not** burn the link, because better-auth checks both lengths before it looks the token up; a no-token screen that blames email clients cutting long links rather than the person; and no sideways scroll at 360px in any of the three states. **The trick recorded on the sign-up row above needs a limit put on it, and it is important.** `127.0.0.1:3021` gives a genuine signed-out render because the session cookie is scoped to `localhost`. It also serves a page that **never hydrates**: React attaches no fiber to anything on that address, so the notice bar close does nothing, the form submits natively and reloads, and every client-wired attribute reads null. That is how issue 836 came to file an upstream silicaui ask claiming `PasswordInput` drops `aria-describedby`. Re-measured on the same page and the same token, `localhost` wires it and `127.0.0.1` does not. The ask is withdrawn. **Read on `127.0.0.1`; measure anything the browser does after load on `localhost`.** Design 8: the shell, the wash, the assurance strip and the deliberate absence of a marketing panel are all right, and the no-token screen is genuinely thoughtful. Ease 6 before, because the two screens that fail are the two a locked-out owner actually meets. Not a 10 yet: the happy path still cannot be driven here without taking the persona's own credential, so the success branch is read rather than clicked. | getpiggles — onboarding                     | 8      | 4 → 9         | The form itself is good and the route around it was not guarded at all. Devi finished setting up on **2026-08-23**; a month later `/onboarding` still opened for her, **prefilled with her live business name and her live web address**, under "We set it all up for you" and a **Take me in** button. Pressing it rewrites `settings.rail` from the tick boxes, re-runs furnishing (whose sample load **clears its prior rows** before writing fresh ones), and **claims a different web address** if the field is edited — on a screen whose own file says the address is asked there "because it can never be here again: an address is an identifier". Her seven sites hang off `juniper-row` (issue 838). The fact that would have stopped it was already being written and read by nobody: `settings.piggles.onboardedAt`, in the same row the page was already loading. **Six of the eight Piggles businesses carry one.** The guard runs in ONE direction on purpose, and the measurement is why: a marker present proves setup finished, a marker absent proves nothing, because a tenant built by a seed never passes through the action that writes it. Wildroot Flowers has no marker, a trade, a real address and a working site — the symmetric rule would have forced a going concern into a setup form. `onboardedAt` also moved to AFTER furnishing returns, so it means "this business is ready" rather than "somebody pressed the button"; otherwise a reload after a furnishing failure would bounce her off the only screen that can finish the job, with her modules still off. Separately, **a Google signup never met setup at all**: the button passed `next="/"`, and `/` sends a signed-in person to `/account`, so that path landed on the account home with the placeholder name, a generated address, no trade, no sample data and **no modules switched on**. The password path beside it redirects to `/onboarding`. Latent rather than live: all eight accounts today were made with a password. What the screen gets right is genuinely good. Three questions, and the file says why there are only three: sparx fills this time asking which modules you want because modules are what it bills for, and Piggles has nothing to sell here. The tick boxes **hide and never gate**, and the action backs the sentence by deliberately not sending `modules` at all. The rail preview **counts what it draws** (`apps.filter(...).length`) rather than carrying a typed number, which is the exact fault issue 835 found in 42 places elsewhere. Every field is keyed on the attempt, because React resets a form after an action and writes back only what changed (issue 163). A field error shows on the field and not also above the form. Design 8. Ease 4 before: nothing on the screen was hard, but the one route into it could quietly cost a business its address and its rows. Not 10: the live read was one pass taken before the guard landed, because lifting the marker to look again is a write to the shared database and the sandbox refused it, correctly. | The rail and app panels                     | 9      | 7 → 9         | The best-built thing in the console, and the two things I thought were wrong with it were not. `getComputedStyle` said the current app's row had a transparent background and the same white text as every other row, on the real element AND on a bare probe — a textbook RULE #4 failure. **The screenshot shows it clearly highlighted.** Then `getBoundingClientRect` said the rail stays 256px wide when collapsed, which would mean collapsing gives back nothing. **The screenshot shows a narrow icon strip with the content filling the width.** Twice in one surface. In this console, read the pixels (issue 839). What IS wrong is small and real: the rail row carried `aria-label={entry.label}`, and `aria-label` **replaces** a control's contents rather than adding to them, so **Invoices 9** on screen announced "Invoices". The count is the only thing on the rail that changes during the day, and it was drawn for one kind of person and withheld from another. Now "Invoices, 9 waiting", with the raw number rather than the badge's `99+`. The label cannot just be dropped: collapsed, the rail is 60px of icons with nothing else to say. The other two `WaitingBadge` call sites carry no `aria-label`, so their counts were already spoken — checked rather than assumed, and only the one place changed. Pulling on the rail's own first row, **Favorites**, found the bigger thing. The visible string was American and everything around it was not: **63 British spellings across 19 files** (`FAVOURITES_LIST`, `favouriteKeys`, `favourited`), against a house rule that names this exact word. Three left alone on purpose: a search-keyword list that carries both spellings so a British customer finds the surface, a tenant's own column name in a fixture, and a Mailchimp CSV header. And `check:american-spelling` had passed the whole time, because its `TREES` were the SHARED server and not the brands' own apps — a guard whose own header says it exists because a rule was "applied to one of the places it holds", doing exactly that. Widened, it went from 2,291 files to **5,549** and from 100,330 pieces of copy to **309,970**, and found **50 British spellings on pages customers read**. The sharpest: sparx's `payment-methods.ts` still labelled the stored value `check` as **Cheque** — the line piggles fixed as issue 384, with the reason written in the file, two months ago. Everything else here holds up. `aria-current` on the browsed app; each row tooltipped with its app's purpose; the panel is `<aside aria-label="Money navigation">` so you know which list you are in; sections fold per device with three states rather than two; Favorites' empty state says "Star any screen to keep it here."; the collapse toggle renames itself to Expand. Design 9, and it earns it. Ease 7 before, only because the one number on the rail was silent. | P03 site — Juniper Row                      | 5 → 8  | 5 → 8         | Twenty-three pages walked as a stranger. **The type carries it**: one serif display face, a real measure, and her amber `#c77618` doing the work on every button and link. It holds at 390px with no sideways scroll on any page, and the words are the best thing on it — the size guide answers "between two sizes" before it is asked, Shipping and returns states the $9 plainly, and Contact promises a same-day reply from the one person who would send it. **Both scores were capped by the same thing, and it was the pictures.** Her shop front sold a $58 "square of silk twill, hand-rolled at the edges" over a photograph of a hank of knitting wool; her Collections page was seven grey placeholder tiles; and "Caring for knitwear so it lasts" was illustrated with hands crumpling paper towels. Four of the seven groups were also EMPTY — seeded from a blueprint whose sample products she had since deleted, so a shopper opening The knitwear edit on a shop that sells a knit was told "Nothing in this collection yet." All fixed as her: a real photograph on every product and every group, her own products in every group, and [338] so the description she writes for a photo is read on the CARD and not only on the product page. **Two of the six gaps are now closed at the platform.** [339] fixed the journal's 128px step — `articleBody()` was narrowing the BAND rather than capping the measure on its content, which is what the rest of that file already did; her blog page stores no tree, so the factory fix reaches her live posts. [340] fixed the reach rule that should have caught the unlinked /collections and did not: it borrowed `BUILTIN_PATHS` (the addresses that EXIST) to answer whether anything REACHES one, exempting all three seeded browse indexes. Her pre-publish check now reports it in her own words, and new sites carry the link in the footer. **Gap to 10, what remains.** (1) Alignment has no rule ACROSS the starter set, and the worst instance of it is now closed. Measured on her About page: the footer's columns started at 703px and her words at **943px**, because that page was the only one on the site set to `max-w-2xl` where four others use `max-w-6xl` — 240px of disagreement with her own header and footer. Fixed on her page (band at the site's measure, prose held at `max-w-2xl` inside it, the structure her own Made in the studio page already used) AND at the platform, because the reason she could never have found it herself was [348]: the control that sets the width showed six plain buttons with nothing marked whenever the value came from a smaller size, which is nearly always. What is still open is the CONVENTION — the starter's bands run `max-w-xl` through `max-w-6xl` with nothing choosing between them, and that is a design decision for the starter set rather than a bug fix. (2) — closed: About was two paragraphs and no photograph on a site whose entire argument is that one person sews the clothes. Rebuilt as her: 1,550 bytes to 10,047, one section to four, no pictures to three. **The studio on Larimer Street** with a photograph of her folded cloth and a real link into How it's made; **There are two of us** naming her and Ines with the work photographs, truthful alt text, and the sample third person deleted; **Where to next** carrying three live links. Opening it as her is also what turned up [346], [347] and [349] — the studio announcing her shop as "Built for the work" for a beat on every page open, Insert burying every group written in her language behind 118 rows of Container and Overflow List and App Shell, and the canvas rendering `src=""` while refusing a bound product photo because `img` is a void tag. (3) — closed: Collections AND Categories are now linked from her footer, added as her through the very remedy the finding prints; her live Explore column reads Shop · Collections · Categories · How it's made · Journal · About · Contact · Search · Size guide · Shipping and returns, and her pre-publish check went 16 → 14. **New this pass, from Brandon's correction that the browse pages are three different jobs rather than duplicates:** her shop had filters and NO WAY TO SEARCH IT on any surface, now fixed ([341]); her Size filter ran S, M, L, XS, XL although she declared the right order ([342], **fixed** — a public `option-axes` read now carries her declared ladder to all four browse surfaces, merged across products topologically because a position only means something inside the product that set it; her Knitwear page reads XS, S, M, L, XL); and `/category` cold-loaded in another company's brand primary rather than her amber ([343], **fixed** — and it was two causes: a failed theme fetch was indistinguishable from having no theme, AND the theme it fell back to was one product's flagship look on a renderer that serves both brands. The base is silicaui's own neutral now, a failed read is retried and then logged, and a live un-themed Piggles shop contains the other brand's hex zero times where it used to carry it on every page). (4) — closed: the product page's hero photograph was `loading="lazy"`, so the largest thing above the fold was the last thing requested ([345], fixed). silicaui's `Image` atom ignores a `loading` prop entirely, so both LCP heroes are raw `img` now while every card stays lazy; her journal post took the fix immediately and the stored product tree is repaired by a heal whose recognizer was measured across all 13 stored trees before it was trusted. (5) — closed at the platform: the studio address and Thursday hours on Contact were set at 14px, in the `caption()` slot the enquiry section reserves for "or call us". A fair size for a phone number and not for the only address on the site, and the slot is the OTHER WAY TO REACH THE BUSINESS whatever an owner writes in it ([344], fixed — with seven more of the same shape across the kit: delivery cost, what a price includes, "call ahead", "Outside these? Call us", an allergy instruction). Her own Contact page is a stored tree and a cohort of ONE (1 page in 419), so it was fixed by hand rather than by fleet repair code — and the issue's claim that she could not have done that herself was wrong. The Design panel's **Text → Size** row rides exactly the `text-sm` / `text-base` ladder, so the repair was one click, keeping her heading, her paragraph and her sentence. It had to be made at the PHONE size: on desktop the row read “Small — from a smaller size”, and clicking there would have left every phone visitor on 14px. Reading that off the chips is [348] working an hour after it shipped. Live at **16px**, matching the paragraph above it. **Then her Contact FORM was tested rather than looked at, and it was a black hole.** A sizing question sent through it as a shopper reached nothing: zero network calls from a clean load, `data-sui-state=“success”`, the text still in the boxes, and `form_submissions` holding three rows that belong to another tenant. The shelf's shared `form()` helper shipped the host ref `'submit'`, which the storefront routes nowhere, and an unrecognised ref is an error at no layer ([350]) — so every form on every tenant site swallowed every enquiry and thanked the sender. Separately the visitor was told nothing either way, the behavior's default confirmation being a 1x1px clipped live region ([351]). And repairing the 29 stored pages found that `upgradePageBody` **was called by nothing at all**, which had also silently voided [345]'s hero repair ([352]). All three fixed; **the end-to-end proof on her live site is still owed** — api-rest was down when the work finished, so her stored page still carries the dead ref and no message has yet been watched landing in her inbox. What is otherwise left in this row is (1)'s convention, which is a design call. **2026-09-01, the shop walked as a customer, and the two biggest finds of the whole run are here.** [371]: **the Quantity box in every buy box was frozen at 1** — typing, the spinner arrows and the up-arrow key all did nothing, so nobody could buy two of anything on any shop on the platform. HTML's `value` (where a control starts) walked into React's `value` (what it is pinned to), and a pinned field with no `onChange` never moves. The older renderer already handled it with a comment and a test; the newer silica walk inherited neither, and `wizeworks/apps/site` was the one app in the repo with no test seat. Fixed, seat added, 19 tests. Confirmed by buying three. [370]: her **Last chance** shelf — the only rule-driven one — was empty while her console said a size had run out, through four faults ending in the indexer skipping every variant-keyed event because it read `productId` off payloads that carry only `variantId`. Fixed; the shelf shows the product. **Otherwise the site holds up well.** All 21 footer links resolve and all six legal pages carry 2,300 to 2,600 words; Home, Shop and a product page have no sideways scroll at 360px and the mobile drawer carries the full nav; a keyboard-only purchase completes with the focus ring visible throughout; her structured data emits Organization and WebSite with a SearchAction; and the footer's facts match her Contact page. Her own writing remains the best thing on it — the made-to-order notice on the Marlow Knit states the ready date, the days needed, and that no card is charged. New gap: [373] five of her titles print the business name twice, because the SEO preview did not show the suffix the site adds; and [375] three of her legal pages still carry the starter's invented numbers, one of which contradicts her own shipping page. **2026-09-01, the site's own search — [378].** A customer typing _returns_ into her search box was told **"No results for 'returns'"** and offered **Browse all products**, on a site whose footer links a Return Policy, a Returns page and a Shipping and returns page; _privacy_, _knitwear_ and _fabric_ the same. Products were found perfectly, so nothing looked broken. The `entities` index held 30 documents platform-wide and **not one was a page or an article**: the `cms_page` projector read the deprecated `Page` model, which has zero rows on the whole database, and articles indexed as `cms_entry`, which the public type list did not include. The strip to show them was already built and already called. Fixed at both ends, plus the page then telling the shopper two opposite things at once. Now _knitwear_ returns her collection, her article and the Marlow Knit, and _returns_ returns her Return Policy. **Builder pages are still in no index** — searching _Larimer_, her studio address on About and Contact, still finds nothing, and that is the larger half of the same shape. **The account area, walked as her customer.** All nine sub-pages load, Orders lists four with semantic status badges, and Returns shows an approved return with a plain instruction. One layout fault, measured rather than eyeballed: the customer's own email address was painted **11px over** the sentence in the next column — 267px of text in a 196px box, because an email has no space to wrap at and the sidebar fits about 22 characters, so it hit most real addresses rather than long ones ([379], fixed with `break-all` + `min-w-0`, not truncation). | P09 site — The Marrow Review                | 2      | 4             | **2026-09-25, act 294.** Live again after the subscription fix, and walked as a stranger. **It is not the magazine’s website. It is the starter, untouched, on a paid public site.** The home page says “Your work, beautifully online” and “This is your homepage; edit every word to make it yours”; About says “Replace this text with a few honest sentences about your work”; the Journal of a reader-funded magazine of ideas carries three Piggles marketing articles under its own name (“How to launch your online store in a weekend”); and the shop sells thirteen ACTIVE sample products — Enamel Pin, Sticker Pack, Ceramic Mug — with working Add to cart. A stranger learns nothing about the business and can buy a pin from a literary review. **Scored as a site, that is a 2.** The starter ITSELF is well built and that is the other half of the reading: no sideways scroll at 390px on any page, nothing wider than the screen, real product cards with real prices, a working 404, and a nav that hides what the tenant does not have — `/wholesale` is a published page that correctly 404s and correctly is not linked, because B2B is off. **One real defect found here and fixed** ([848](issues/848-the-shopper-read-the-html.md)): every sample product printed its own HTML to the shopper — `<p>A hard enamel pin…</p><p>About 1.25 inches…</p>` as the sentence on the page — because all eleven sample-data packs write markup into a field the console edits in a bare textarea and the site renders as plain text. Measured: **185 of 577 product descriptions on this machine, across 9 businesses**. Fixed in the packs (536 tags) AND at the render, because a source fix reaches the next install and never the shops already open. **848 left a note listing four other readers of that column and stopped there, which is a defect parked as a measurement; that is now closed** ([850](issues/850-one-line-said-html-was-allowed-and-five-readers-disagreed.md)). The line underneath all of it was in the schema: `description: z.string().max(50_000).nullish(), // rich text (HTML allowed)`, while the console edits it in a bare textarea, the site renders it as text and there is no rich-text editor for it anywhere. It now normalizes on parse. The four readers: **both consoles** stripped tags with `/<[^>]*>/g`, which ate the words between an ordinary `<` and `>` so an owner writing “fits anything < 3 inches across, weighs > 2oz” lost her own sentence in the search preview; **the search index** stored the raw column, making `strong` and `li` searchable words; **dropship imports** wrote Printful and DSers HTML straight in past the schema, and showed it in the preview too; **the public API** served it raw to every headless client. No email template reads it, so that entry on the list was wrong. `plainText` moved out of the site app into `@wizeworks/commerce-schemas`, which all four trees already depended on, so five callers now share one function. The true count is **188 of 577**, not 185: `LIKE '%</p>%'` missed three rows carrying only `<br>`, `<strong>` or `<li>`. The repair script is written, dry-run against the real database, and deliberately not applied. **The second defect was filed as a decision and then fixed** ([849](issues/849-a-magazine-published-the-platforms-marketing-under-its-own-name.md)): a business that pays and goes live before editing publishes somebody else’s articles and merchandise under its own name, and nothing in the product ever said so. Everything needed was already written down — every artifact an install creates is stamped with a baseline, and the updater’s own handlers already read each live row back in that same shape, so “has she touched this?” was answerable and nobody was asking. Home now names what a visitor can still read: her shop is selling Rowan canvas tote and five more, her Journal is publishing three articles written as examples. Only once she has published, one offer at a time, examples before pages, and it changes nothing. The comparison had to be measured twice — a strict compare read three column defaults (`tags: []`, `fulfillmentType`, `requiresShipping`) as her edits and reported nothing at all. | P03 — the shopper's account, after the sale | 5 → 8  | 3 → 8         | Design: the order page was already the good part — a real status timeline, the carrier and a live tracking link, the address, the totals. It lost three black rules across the status card ([293]) and a list that rendered as a centered stack ([294]), and gained a refund line that tells her what she actually paid ([292]). **Ease moved twice.** The header now knows her ([291]) instead of offering to sign in a signed-in customer, and — the big one — **she can send something back herself** ([297]): pick the lines, say why, ask for money or a swap, and follow it, on a business where returns are 22% of orders. What is left: the orders list still names an order by number, date and total only, so finding the right one among many means opening each. **Re-scored on 2026-08-28**, and the ceiling on both was money: her order page showed a price nobody had quoted her ([298]) until the discount reached the order, and it now names what came off each item the way the console does. On a phone the whole area opened on a 635px menu with her order below it ([299]) — 359px now. Held at 356px with no horizontal overflow. What is left is unchanged: the orders list still names an order by number, date and total only. | P03 — Cart → Checkout, as the shopper       | 6 → 8  | 4 → 8         | The three steps read well and the copy is honestly good — "Once we know where" for a shipping line it cannot know yet, "Placing this order does not take any money now", the made-to-order date carried the whole way. Both scores were capped by the same thing: **the money on screen was not the money written down.** The button said $129.20 and the order said $152.00 ([298]); an ended sale went on being honored right through it ([300]); a code typed after checkout began never counted, and one step showed the saving while the next did not ([301]). All three fixed, and the button's own total is now sent back so nothing is written for a figure she was not shown. Gap to 10: the review page never re-reads, so the label can sit stale until she presses it — the press is caught and refused, but she finds out at the button rather than before it. | Checkout, as a shopper                      | 6 → 9  | 5 → 9         | **2026-09-25, act 292.** The whole sale walked six times end to end, signed in as Marguerite, at 1280px and at 390px, with real orders at the end of each. The copy is the best thing about it and it is genuinely good — “Once we know where” for a line that cannot be known yet, “Placing this order does not take any money now, and no card details are needed”, and a pay button that says the amount (**Place order: $51.00 to pay**). Prefill works, `autocomplete` is right on all three fields, and at 390px the summary moves ABOVE the form so she sees what she is buying before she types. Five defects, all fixed the same act ([846](issues/846-the-total-went-backwards-when-she-did.md)). The one that matters: she ticks **Delivery · 4 days $9.00** and the summary beside it goes on saying **Once we know where** and **Total so far $42.00**, then the payment step says **$51.00**, then **← Back** drops it to **$42.00** again with the $9.00 still ticked — the number moved backwards when she did, and on a phone the stale total is the FIRST thing on the screen. One flag, `settled`, was answering two questions; it now answers one and the chosen rate answers the other, in a tested module that goes red on exactly the three cases the old code got wrong. Her usual address printed the same street twice and lost her name, because the fallback chain ended in the address while the name sat two functions up in the same file; and an `aria-label` on each row REPLACED its contents, so **“your usual one”** — the single fact telling the three rows apart — was on the screen and in nobody’s ears (issue 839’s shape again). The phone field was named with its own help sentence. **The confirmation carried a heading, an order number and Continue shopping** — not what she bought, not what it cost, not where it was going, and no link to the order, whose id `placeOrder` returns and checkout dropped one line later; on a shop that takes money in person no email follows either, so that screen was the whole record of the sale. And `/checkout` with an empty basket gave the full form, a $0.00 total and a submit button stuck on **Saving…** forever, because “no cart id” was read as “still loading”. **Gap to 10:** checkout calls the rate **Delivery** and the order page calls it **Standard Delivery**, ten seconds apart; the guest path is unwalked, and a guest still has nothing to come back to; the marketing checkbox is a 24px tap target. ## How this list was built

```
node piggles/scripts/gen-pane-ratings.mjs
```

Generated rather than typed, from three sources — because a pane is only what a
person can actually open and read:

| Source                      | Gives                                                       |
| --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `lib/surfaces/catalog/*.ts` | every registered surface                                    |
| `lib/console/vocabulary.ts` | what Piggles **calls** it — 99 of the 323 are renamed there |
| `lib/console/product.tsx`   | `hiddenSurfaces`, which are not Piggles panes at all        |

Grouped by app through `modules` and `claims` in `packages/config/src/apps.ts`,
so Partners shows the supplier screens it claims from Stock.

**The names here are the ones on screen, not the catalog's.** sparx calls
`commerce.carts.list` "Carts"; a Piggles owner reads "Baskets left behind", and
rating a screen means rating the words on it.

**Regenerate when the catalog changes** — before a run, never during one. A pane
added after this file was written is a pane nobody is asked to rate, and a
missing row reads as a covered one. The rubric above the marker survives a
regeneration; scores inside the generated block do not.
